plans.note: Section 21 is the operative cap; check mutuality, cap quantum versus fees paid, exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, and whether 'Excluded Claims' (defined in sec-1) properly carves out IP indemnity, confidentiality, data breach and wilful misconduct. Cross-check sec-20 for uncapped indemnity treatment.

Section 20 should carry Vendor's third-party IP infringement indemnity plus indemnity for its negligence/wilful misconduct and data breach; confirm any Customer-side indemnity is narrow (Customer Data lawfulness/misuse only) and that defence, control and cost allocation are workable. Interaction with sec-21 carve-outs matters.

No dedicated restrictive-covenant section in the outline; scan scope (sec-2), Customer responsibilities (sec-12), licence restrictions (sec-13) and General (sec-30) for any restraint on Customer's business, products it may build, or competing offerings. Expect absent.

Look for 'sole source', 'exclusive provider' or all-requirements language in the agreement structure/scope (sec-2), Order Form mechanics (sec-4) and Customer obligations (sec-12). Likely absent, but Order Form provisions can smuggle exclusivity.
Check pricing/fees (sec-7) and Order Forms (sec-4) for any obligation on Customer to extend best terms to Vendor; an MFN running in Customer's favour is beneficial and must not be flagged.

Non-solicits are commonly buried in General (sec-30) or near Customer responsibilities (sec-12). If present, test duration (12 months preferred), mutuality, limitation to personnel actually engaged on the Services, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-response carve-out.

Section 9 is the termination hub: confirm Customer may terminate for convenience on reasonable notice without early-termination or unwinding penalties, and that Vendor has no reciprocal mid-term convenience right. Read with term (sec-8) and effects/refunds (sec-10).

Section 8 governs auto-renewal: check renewal term length, non-renewal notice window (30 days preferred, 60 acceptable) and any uplift on renewal pricing in sec-8 or sec-7. A missing uplift cap alone is a rationale note, not a deviation.

Section 28 covers governing law, venue and any arbitration. Vendor is a UK entity, so watch for England and Wales (accepted) versus an off-list law or foreign-seated arbitration; also check exclusive jurisdiction and any jury/injunctive carve-outs.

Section 24 is on point: confirm Customer may assign to Affiliates and to a successor in merger/asset sale without consent, and that Vendor has no termination right on Customer's change of control; check any Vendor assignment/subcontracting rights and residual boilerplate in sec-30.

Section 14 should vest Deliverables in Customer (or at minimum grant a broad perpetual licence) and sec-15 should confirm Customer owns Customer Data; verify no assignment of Customer IP/data to Vendor and that any feedback or aggregated-data licence to Vendor is limited and de-identified. Definitions in sec-1 control scope.

Section 13 grants the access rights: test that the licence extends to Affiliates and contractors acting for Customer, is non-revocable during the term (suspension only for defined cause), and that use restrictions in sec-13/sec-12 do not narrow it below the fallback.

Section 22 likely contains Vendor's audit of Customer usage: check frequency (no more than annual), advance written notice, business-hours/off-site-where-possible conduct, confidentiality, and Vendor bearing cost absent material underpayment. Section 23 may hold reciprocal Customer assurance rights that should not be traded away.

Check sec-7 for late-payment interest or early-termination/liquidated sums payable by Customer and sec-3 for SLA service credits (credits to us are beneficial and must not be flagged). Only Customer-payable penalties are a deviation; avoid double-flagging any early-termination fee also raised under T4C.

Section 19 holds the warranties: test the services/deliverables conformity warranty, its duration, and whether the remedy is real (re-performance then refund) rather than sole-remedy repair only. Read with acceptance testing (sec-6) and performance/SLA obligations (sec-3); note any broad disclaimer of implied warranties.

Section 18 should set Vendor's coverages; verify commercial general liability, professional indemnity/E&O and cyber limits, certificate delivery and notice of cancellation given Vendor hosts Customer Data (cross-refer sec-15, sec-17).

Look in fees (sec-7) and Order Form/Affiliate order mechanics (sec-4) for minimum volume or take-or-pay commitments, non-reducible seat counts, or ratchets on renewal (sec-8); acceptable only with a proportional exit or true-down right.

Section 11 is the transition/data-return clause: confirm a defined assistance period, continuation of Services at then-current rates, export of Customer Data in a usable format at no or reasonable cost, and deletion certification. Cross-check sec-10 for any data-destruction or fee-conditionality that undercuts it.
